Mission

The Chair of Operations, Economics and Strategy (OES) at the College of Management of Technology at EPFL invites applications for a full-time PhD student position within the EPFL doctoral school program in Management of Technology (EDMT).

We are offering a challenging full-time PhD student position at the Chair of Operations, Economics and Strategy (OES) at EPFL.

The mission of OES is to conduct world-class research and teaching at the intersection of operations, economics, and strategy, with a focus on organizations and their interactions.

At OES, you will have the opportunity to work on the design, analysis, and implementation of innovative models for decision-making, economics, and operations. Research topics may include optimization, decision-making under uncertainty, market design and pricing, operations research, dynamic systems, and strategy-relevant applications.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop and complete an original doctoral dissertation

• Conduct independent research in close interaction with the Chair and, where appropriate, with external or industry partners

• Contribute to teaching activities, including co-supervision of student projects

• Provide limited support for academic and administrative activities of the Chair

Profile

• An excellent Master’s-level degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Economics, Industrial Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field

• A strong mathematical background, including familiarity with optimization, probability, and the analysis of mathematical models

• A sincere interest in business-related, economic, and operational problems

• Proficiency in English

• Strong motivation for academic research, critical thinking, independence, good self-management skills, and team spirit

• Interest in a career involving research and teaching is an asset

We offer

• Excellent working conditions in an international research environment

• Individual and intensive supervision of your PhD project

• Financial support in accordance with EPFL doctoral student conditions

• The opportunity to work on rigorous, practically relevant research at the interface of operations, economics, and strategy

Informations

Your application should include:

• CV

• Motivation letter

• Diplomas

• Transcripts/grades from Bachelor’s and Master’s studies

To be eligible for a PhD at EPFL, candidates must be admitted to an EPFL doctoral school program. For this position, candidates should also apply to the EPFL EDMT Doctoral School :
https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/edmt-management-of-technology/edmt-how-to-apply/

Application deadlines: January 15, 2027 and April 15, 2027. Applications to OES may be reviewed on a rolling basis; formal admission to EDMT requires a complete application by one of these deadlines.

Expected start date: September 1st, 2027. An alternative start date may exceptionally be agreed upon by mutual agreement.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Mission La Chaire d'exploitation, d'économie et de stratégie (OES) du Collège de gestion de la technologie de l'EPFL invite les candidats à un poste de doctorant à temps plein au sein du programme d'études doctorales de l'EPFL en gestion de la technologie (EDMT). Nous offrons un poste de doctorant à temps plein à la Chaire d'opérations, d'économie et de stratégie (OES) de l'EPFL. La mission de l'OES est de mener des recherches et de l'enseignement de calibre mondial à l'intersection des opérations, de l'économie et de la stratégie, en mettant l'accent sur les organisations et leurs interactions. Chez OES, vous aurez l'occasion de travailler sur la conception, l'analyse et la mise en œuvre de modèles innovants pour la prise de décision, l'économie et les opérations. Les sujets de recherche peuvent inclure l'optimisation, la prise de décisions dans le cadre de l'incertitude, la conception et la tarification du marché, la recherche opérationnelle, les systèmes dynamiques et les applications stratégiques. • Élaborer et compléter une thèse de doctorat originale
• Mener des recherches indépendantes en étroite collaboration avec la chaire et, le cas échéant, avec des partenaires extérieurs ou industriels
• Contribuer aux activités d'enseignement, y compris la co-surveillance des projets étudiants
• Apporter un appui limité aux activités universitaires et administratives de la chaire Profil
• Un excellent master en ingénierie, mathématiques appliquées, recherche opérationnelle, économie, génie industriel, mathématiques, informatique, ou un domaine quantitatif connexe
• Un solide contexte mathématique, y compris la familiarité avec l'optimisation, la probabilité et l'analyse des modèles mathématiques
• Un intérêt sincère pour les problèmes commerciaux, économiques et opérationnels
• Compétence en anglais
• Forte motivation pour la recherche académique, la pensée critique, l'indépendance, de bonnes compétences en autogestion et l'esprit d'équipe
• L'intérêt pour une carrière impliquant la recherche et l'enseignement est un atout Nous offrons
• Excellentes conditions de travail dans un environnement de recherche international
• Supervision individuelle et intensive de votre projet de doctorat
• Soutien financier selon les conditions de doctorants de l'EPFL
• La possibilité de travailler sur des recherches rigoureuses et pratiquement pertinentes à l'interface des opérations, de l'économie et de la stratégie Informations Votre demande devrait comprendre:
• CV
• Lettre de motivation
• Diplômes
• Transcriptions/grades des études de baccalauréat et de maîtrise Pour être éligible à un doctorat à l'EPFL, les candidats doivent être admis à un programme d'études doctorales de l'EPFL. Pour ce poste, les candidats doivent également postuler à l'Ecole EPFL EDMT Doctorale : https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/edmt-management-of-technology/edmt-how-to-apply/ Dates limites de présentation des demandes : 15 janvier 2027 et 15 avril 2027. Les demandes à l'OES peuvent être examinées sur une base continue; l'admission officielle à l'EDMT exige une demande complète dans l'un de ces délais. Date de début prévue : 1er septembre 2027. Une autre date de début peut exceptionnellement être convenue d'un commun accord. Seuls les candidats présélectionnés seront contactés.

titleByLocale.fr: Postdoctoral Researcher

jobs.description:
Mission

Despite recent technological advances both in the data management and in computer architecture domains, our ability to analyze data still falls behind the unstoppable data collection rates. Data-intensive applications are increasingly more demanding in sophisticated algorithms to store, manage, and interpret data. To meet the challenges, database software needs to communicate efficiently both with the application layer and with the underlying hardware platforms, and deliver seamless computational and data management support. Research in the DIAS lab addresses both aspects of the challenge: we adapt data management technology to computer architecture trends by designing data manipulation techniques that exploit optimally the underlying hardware and I/O devices, and we enable new discoveries in scientific domains through automating physical database design and revolutionizing exploration algorithms in very large data repositories. The DIAS lab pioneers just-in-time query engines which support analytics on raw data, data cleaning and query optimization for heterogeneous distributed data, and hardware/software codesigned engines for demanding applications.

Main duties and responsibilities

•
Work closely with all members of the lab carrying out excellent research

•
Supervise students and collaborate with other postdocs

•
(optional) Contribute to teaching (especially if interested in an academic career)

Profile

•
Highly motivated with proven scientific excellence in the areas of vector query processing, serverless/just-in-time query execution, parallel and distributed data management, and data management systems on emerging hardware

•
Passionate about inventing, building, and publishing quality database systems research

•
A strong publication record and hands-on experience in system development are especially important

We offer

• The DIAS Lab team is renowned for its collaborative and nourishing culture, which supports the lab’s members since their first day in the team and long after their departure

•
Excellent working conditions

•
The contract is fixed for one year initially, renewable up to four years

Informations

Interested parties should send an application through the system including a CV, a research statement, and the names of at least three references. For inquiries regarding the research aspects of the position, contact Prof. Anastasia Ailamaki .

Contract Start Date : 01/01/2026

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type : CDD

Duration: 1-year fixed-term contract, renewable

titleByLocale.en: PhD student position -Interfacial Imaging of Membrane Water
titleByLocale.fr: Poste d'étudiant au doctorat - Imagerie interculturelle de l'eau de membrane

jobs.description:
Mission

We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student at School of Engineering - STI at EPFL. At the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics - LBP we are developing nonlinear imaging techniques to study, characterize and image water in different configuration.

Introduction

Water is the liquid of life. It is intimately linked to our well-being. Without water, cell membranes cannot function. Charges and charged groups cannot be dissolved, self-assembly cannot occur, and proteins cannot fold. That water is intimately linked with life, we experience time and again when we quench our thirst, but how does this link work?

Osmosis is the flow of water across a (cell) membrane that separates two aqueous solutions with different concentrations of a solutes. Regulating osmotic pressure is a key survival strategy of cells and plays an important role in the functioning of every organism. How osmotic pressure and cell membrane tension are regulated on the molecular level is not known. It is the aim of the ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, a collaboration between EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) and the University of Geneva (Prof. A. Roux) to work this out. To do so, we will develop new technology and perform experiments in vitro and vivo.

The Project at EPFL – focused on technology development & in vitro studies

Nonlinear optical imaging and new ultrafast spectroscopic techniques have recently been developed in the Roke lab and used to image in real time interfacial water and electrostatic potentials on membrane interfaces of model membranes and in living cells.

We will use second harmonic water imaging to (1) image interfacial water in real time as well as the electrostatic field lines on lipid membrane interface model systems, and (2) image in real time membrane fusion and osmosis. The imaging data will be used to link molecular level information to electrostatics and mechanics of membranes.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:

• Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

• Research in close collaboration with industry partners

• Experiment design and execution

• Analyze and interpret experimental results

• Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals

• Present at international conferences

• Participate in education and supervise student project

This research has many interdisciplinary aspects that demand a highly motivated candidate with strong analytical abilities that is able to think out of the box. The diverse aspects of the project allow a wide range of backgrounds that should include photonics, physics, chemistry/material science, electrical or bioengineering. Experience in nonlinear optics / microscopy, or ultrafast spectroscopy is a bonus. We offer excellent working conditions and a state-of-the-art infrastructure in a highly dynamic and international environment at the forefront of research.

Profile

• A MSc degree

• Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team

• Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eager to learn, good organizational skills, rigor in experimental work

• High level of motivation for academic research work

• Fluency in English is essential, French / German / Italian would be an asset

We offer

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• An opportunity to develop a scientific career

• A world-class research and training environment with access to state-of-the-art research facilities

• A multi-cultural and stimulating work environment

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, photonics, materials science, or electrical engineering.
Please check this page for additional information on admission.

Please note that this is a separate application process necessary t

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione Stiamo offrendo una posizione impegnativa come uno studente di dottorato a tempo pieno (100%) a Scuola di Ingegneria - STI a EPFL. Al Laboratorio per BioPhotonics fondamentali - LBP stiamo sviluppando tecniche di imaging non lineare per studiare, caratterizzare e immagine acqua in diversa configurazione. Introduzione L'acqua è il liquido della vita. È intimamente legata al nostro benessere. Senza acqua, le membrane cellulari non possono funzionare. Le spese e i gruppi carichi non possono essere dissolti, l'auto-assemblaggio non può verificarsi e le proteine non possono piegarsi. Che l'acqua è intimamente legata alla vita, sperimentiamo tempo e di nuovo quando sperimentiamo la nostra sete, ma come funziona questo collegamento? L'osmosi è il flusso d'acqua attraverso una membrana (cell) che separa due soluzioni acquose con diverse concentrazioni di un soluto. Regolare la pressione osmotica è una strategia chiave di sopravvivenza delle cellule e svolge un ruolo importante nel funzionamento di ogni organismo. Come la pressione osmotica e la tensione della membrana cellulare sono regolate a livello molecolare non è noto. È l'obiettivo della ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, una collaborazione tra EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) e l'Università di Ginevra (Prof. A. Roux) per risolvere questo problema. Per farlo, svilupperemo una nuova tecnologia e faremo esperimenti in vitro e vivo. Il progetto EPFL – focalizzato sullo sviluppo tecnologico e gli studi in vitro L'imaging ottico non lineare e le nuove tecniche spettroscopiche ultraveloci sono state recentemente sviluppate nel laboratorio Roke e utilizzate per l'immagine in tempo reale dell'acqua interfacciale e dei potenziali elettrostatici sulle interfacce a membrana delle membrane dei modelli e nelle cellule viventi. Useremo la seconda immagine armonica dell'acqua a (1) immagine dell'acqua interfacciale in tempo reale, così come le linee di campo elettrostatiche sui sistemi di interfaccia della membrana lipidica modello, e (2) immagine in tempo reale fusione e osmosi della membrana. I dati di imaging saranno utilizzati per collegare le informazioni a livello molecolare agli elettrostatici e alla meccanica delle membrane. Principali doveri e responsabilità Come studente di dottorato, ci si aspetta di:
• Avere piena responsabilità per la propria dissertazione
• Ricerca in stretta collaborazione con partner industriali
• Progettazione sperimentale ed esecuzione
• Analizzare e interpretare i risultati sperimentali
• Scrivere articoli scientifici per la pubblicazione in riviste peer-reviewed
• Presente alle conferenze internazionali
• Partecipare all'istruzione e supervisionare il progetto degli studenti Questa ricerca ha molti aspetti interdisciplinari che richiedono un candidato altamente motivato con forti capacità analitiche che è in grado di pensare fuori dalla scatola. I diversi aspetti del progetto permettono una vasta gamma di sfondi che dovrebbero includere fotonici, fisica, chimica/scienza materiale, elettrico o bioingegneria. Esperienza in ottica non lineare / microscopia, o spettroscopia ultraveloce è un bonus. Offriamo eccellenti condizioni di lavoro e un'infrastruttura all'avanguardia in un ambiente altamente dinamico e internazionale all'avanguardia della ricerca. Profilo
• Un grado MSc
• Buona capacità di comunicazione e disponibilità a lavorare come parte di un team
• Enthusiasm, curiosità scientifica, desideroso di imparare, buone capacità organizzative, rigore nel lavoro sperimentale
• Alto livello di motivazione per il lavoro di ricerca accademica
• La fluenza in inglese è essenziale, francese / tedesco / italiano sarebbe un bene Offriamo
• 4 anni per completare il dottorato con una remunerazione competitiva
• Un'opportunità per sviluppare una carriera scientifica
• Un ambiente di ricerca e formazione di livello mondiale con accesso a strutture di ricerca all'avanguardia
• Un ambiente di lavoro multiculturale e stimolante
• Un contratto a tempo determinato di 1 anno (CDD), rinnovabile per 4 anni Informazioni Il processo di selezione coinvolge più fasi, e candidati a lista corta sarà richiesto di applicare a un programma specifico di dottorato EPFL per qualificarsi per un dottorato in EPFL, fotonici, scienza dei materiali o ingegneria elettrica. Si prega di controllare questa pagina per ulteriori informazioni sull'ammissione. Si prega di notare che questo è un processo di applicazione separato necessario t

We will use second harmonic water imaging to (1) image interfacial water in real time as well as the electrostatic field lines on lipid membrane interface model systems, and (2) image in real time membrane fusion and osmosis. The imaging data will be used to link molecular level information to electrostatics and mechanics of membranes.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Research in close collaboration with industry partners

• Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals

• Present at international conferences

• Participate in education and supervise student project

This research has many interdisciplinary aspects that demand a highly motivated candidate with strong analytical abilities that is able to think out of the box. The diverse aspects of the project allow a wide range of backgrounds that should include photonics, physics, chemistry/material science, electrical or bioengineering. Experience in nonlinear optics / microscopy, or ultrafast spectroscopy is a bonus. We offer excellent working conditions and a state-of-the-art infrastructure in a highly dynamic and international environment at the forefront of research.

Mission Nous offrons un poste difficile comme doctorant à temps plein (100%) à l'École d'ingénierie - STI à l'EPFL. Au Laboratoire de BioPhotonique fondamentale - LBP, nous développons des techniques d'imagerie non linéaire pour étudier, caractériser et imager l'eau dans différentes configurations. Présentation L'eau est le liquide de la vie. Elle est intimement liée à notre bien-être. Sans eau, les membranes cellulaires ne peuvent pas fonctionner. Les charges et les groupes chargés ne peuvent pas être dissous, l'auto-assemblage ne peut pas se produire et les protéines ne peuvent pas se replier. Cette eau est intimement liée à la vie, nous expérimentons à maintes reprises quand nous étanchons notre soif, mais comment fonctionne ce lien? L'osmose est le flux d'eau à travers une membrane (cellule) qui sépare deux solutions aqueuses avec des concentrations différentes d'un soluté. La régulation de la pression osmotique est une stratégie clé de survie des cellules et joue un rôle important dans le fonctionnement de chaque organisme. On ne sait pas comment la pression osmotique et la tension de la membrane cellulaire sont régulées au niveau moléculaire. C'est l'objectif de l'ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, une collaboration entre l'EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) et l'Université de Genève (Prof. A. Roux) pour y parvenir. Pour ce faire, nous allons développer de nouvelles technologies et effectuer des expériences in vitro et vivo. Le projet de l'EPFL – axé sur le développement technologique et les études in vitro L'imagerie optique non linéaire et les nouvelles techniques spectroscopiques ultrarapides ont récemment été développées dans le laboratoire Roke et utilisées pour l'image en temps réel de l'eau interfaciale et des potentiels électrostatiques sur les interfaces membranaires des membranes modèles et dans les cellules vivantes. Nous utiliserons la deuxième imagerie harmonique de l'eau pour (1) l'image de l'eau interfaciale en temps réel ainsi que les lignes de champ électrostatiques sur les systèmes de modèles d'interface membrane lipidique, et (2) l'image en temps réel fusion membrane et osmose. Les données d'imagerie serviront à lier l'information sur le niveau moléculaire à l'électrostatique et à la mécanique des membranes. jobs.description:
Mission

EPFL is one of the most dynamic university campuses in Europe, ranks among the top 20 universities worldwide and offers an exceptional working environment with very competitive salaries. The LTS2 Lab https://lts2.epfl.ch offers a highly motivating, interdisciplinary scientific environment with many opportunities to interact between different projects and researchers, and has an excellent network of collaborative research projects with applications ranging from biology to neuroscience. The objective of this project is to develop groundbreaking generative AI methodologies for the design of novel materials. This is part of a large ERC Synergy project involving de novo simulations, automated experimental platforms driven by AI models. It offers extraordinary opportunites to collaborate with materials scientists on a quest to set-up a new blueprint for materials discovery, from computational approaches to actual synthesis and characterization.

Profile

We are looking for 2 PhD students who will contribute novel multimodal generative AI architectures, latent diffusion processes, and reinforcement learning approaches. Interestingly, the proposed model will interface with an automated platform performing experimental materials synthesis and incorporate data from experimental characterization and simulations.

We are looking for PhD candidates with a strong analytical background, and an outstanding MSc degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. You should be proficient in or willing to learn generative deep learning – in particular based on latent diffusion, multimodal approaches, statistics and learning theory. We expect the candidate to be self-driven with strong problem-solving abilities and out-of-the-box thinking. You are willing to contribute and understand new AI architectures, implement and test them. More importantly, you are willing to partake in a collective international research endeavour involving researchers from different disciplines. Professional command of English (both written and spoken) is mandatory. To be eligible for these positions you must also apply and be accepted to the doctoral program in Electrical Engineering. Please check https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/ for additional information. Please note that this is a separate application process.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:

Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

Research in close collaboration with academic partners;

Experiment design and execution ;

Analyze and interpret experimental results;

Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals;

Present at international conferences.

Supervise student projects

We offer

4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

A world-class research and training environment with access to state-of-the-art research facilities;

A multi-cultural and stimulating work environment;

International collaboration and research internships at other institutions in Belgium and France;

Term of employment: 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years.

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered.

Your application should contain:

• Motivation Letter

• Detailed CV

• Contact information

• At least 2 references willing to write a recommendation letter.

For more information, please contact: pierre.vandergheynst@epfl.ch

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type : PhD Student

Reference : 2048

jobs.description:
Mission

We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student at School of Engineering - STI at EPFL. At the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics - LBP we are developing nonlinear imaging techniques to study, characterize and image water in different configuration.

Introduction

Electrolyte solutions in water are an essential ingredient of many aspects of life and technology: the bodily fluids (blood and cellular fluid are prime examples), but also are the key contents of batteries. The electrolyte in batteries determines the power output, life span and efficient energy storage. Electrolyte solutions are commonly described as homogeneous mixtures in which ions are statistically distributed. However, it is well known from theoretical considerations in the 1930’s that this simple description is incomplete for the relevant concentration range and that the structure of electrolyte solutions is far more complex. Experiments to understand this need to cover time scales ranging from femto- to milliseconds, and length scales from atomistic dimensions to microns, a huge challenge.

The Project at EPFL

We will use various novel home-built technologies based on nonlinear optical scattering and imaging methods to achieve this: second harmonic imaging, angle-resolved-second harmonic scattering, and correlated vibrational spectroscopy, all ultrafast optical methods, supplemented by standard linear spectroscopy and light scattering methods. These methods will be applied to simple 3D electrolytes in water, and 2D electrolyte regions at aqueous interfaces. Linking all datasets will allow to map both short – and long-range interactions and collective effects pertaining to all molecular actors. This allows to solve the puzzle surrounding concentrated electrolyte solutions and how they work, for example in their charge transmitting/storing functions and lead to a better understanding, and ultimately new technology.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:

• Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

• Research in close collaboration with industry partners

• Experiment design and execution

• Analyze and interpret experimental results

• Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals

• Present at international conferences

• Participate in education and supervise student project

This research has many interdisciplinary aspects that demand a highly motivated candidate with strong analytical abilities that can think out of the box. The successful candidate has a background in photonics, physics, chemistry/material science, or electrical engineering, ideally supplemented by hands-on experience in free space optics / microscopy, nonlinear optics or ultrafast spectroscopy. We offer excellent working conditions and a state-of-the-art infrastructure in a highly dynamic and international environment at the forefront of research.

Profile

• A MSc degree

• Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team

• Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eager to learn, good organizational skills, rigor in experimental work

• High level of motivation for academic research work

• Fluency in English is essential, French / German / Italian would be an asset

We offer

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• An opportunity to develop a scientific career

• A world-class research and training environment with access to state-of-the-art research facilities

• A multi-cultural and stimulating work environment

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, photonics, materials science, or electrical engineering.

Al Laboratorio per BioPhotonics fondamentali - LBP stiamo sviluppando tecniche di imaging non lineare per studiare, caratterizzare e immagine acqua in diversa configurazione. Introduzione Le soluzioni elettrolitiche in acqua sono un ingrediente essenziale di molti aspetti della vita e della tecnologia: i fluidi corporei (il sangue e il liquido cellulare sono esempi primi), ma sono anche il contenuto chiave delle batterie. L'elettrolita nelle batterie determina l'uscita di potenza, la durata di vita e l'accumulo di energia efficiente. Le soluzioni elettrolitiche sono comunemente descritte come miscele omogenee in cui gli ioni sono statisticamente distribuiti. Tuttavia, è ben noto da considerazioni teoriche negli anni '30 che questa semplice descrizione è incompleta per la relativa gamma di concentrazione e che la struttura delle soluzioni elettrolitiche è molto più complessa. Esperimenti per capire questa necessità di coprire scale di tempo che vanno da femto a millisecondi, e scale di lunghezza da dimensioni atomiste a micron, una sfida enorme. Il progetto in EPFL Useremo varie nuove tecnologie home-built basate su metodi di spargimento ottico non lineare e di imaging per raggiungere questo obiettivo: seconda imaging armonico, angolo-risolto-secondo spargimento armonico, e spettroscopia vibrazionale correlata, tutti i metodi ottici ultraveloci, integrati da spettroscopia lineare standard e metodi di spargimento della luce. Questi metodi saranno applicati a semplici elettroliti 3D in acqua, e regioni elettrolitiche 2D a interfacce acquose. Collegare tutti i dataset permetterà di mappare sia le interazioni brevi, sia quelle a lungo raggio e gli effetti collettivi relativi a tutti gli attori molecolari. Questo permette di risolvere il puzzle che circonda soluzioni elettrolitiche concentrate e come funzionano, ad esempio nelle loro funzioni di trasmissione / memorizzazione di carica e portare a una migliore comprensione, e in ultima analisi, nuova tecnologia. Il candidato di successo ha uno sfondo in fotonici, fisica, chimica / scienza materiale, o ingegneria elettrica, idealmente integrato da esperienza hands-on in ottica spazio libero / microscopia, ottica non lineare o spettroscopia ultraveloce. Au Laboratoire de BioPhotonique fondamentale - LBP, nous développons des techniques d'imagerie non linéaire pour étudier, caractériser et imager l'eau dans différentes configurations. Présentation Les solutions électrolytiques dans l'eau sont un ingrédient essentiel de nombreux aspects de la vie et de la technologie : les fluides corporels (le sang et le liquide cellulaire en sont des exemples essentiels), mais aussi le contenu clé des batteries. L'électrolyte dans les batteries détermine la puissance, la durée de vie et le stockage efficace de l'énergie. Les solutions électrolytiques sont généralement décrites comme des mélanges homogènes dans lesquels les ions sont répartis statistiquement. Cependant, il est bien connu, d'après les considérations théoriques des années 1930, que cette description simple est incomplète pour la gamme de concentration pertinente et que la structure des solutions d'électrolytes est beaucoup plus complexe. Des expériences pour comprendre ce besoin de couvrir des échelles de temps allant de fem à millisecondes, et des échelles de longueur des dimensions atomistes aux microns, un défi énorme. Le projet à l'EPFL Pour ce faire, nous utiliserons diverses nouvelles technologies maison basées sur des méthodes de diffusion et d'imagerie optiques non linéaires : deuxième imagerie harmonique, diffusion harmonique résolue par angle et seconde, et spectroscopie vibrationnelle corrélée, toutes les méthodes optiques ultrarapides, complétées par des méthodes standard de spectroscopie linéaire et de diffusion de la lumière. Ces méthodes seront appliquées aux électrolytes 3D simples dans l'eau et aux régions électrolytes 2D aux interfaces aqueuses. Lier tous les ensembles de données permettra de cartographier à la fois les interactions à courte et à longue distance et les effets collectifs relatifs à tous les acteurs moléculaires. jobs.description:
Mission

The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch .

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.

Main duties and responsibilities

The project is conducted in collaboration with the Environmental Fluid Mechanics Laboratory ( https://pietrodeanna.org ) at the University of Lausanne, led by Prof. Pietro de Anna, where the experimental work will be carried out, and with the Theoretical Chemistry group at ETH Zurich ( https://reiher.ethz.ch ), led by Prof. Markus Reiher, which will perform detailed quantum-chemical calculations of reaction rates.
The research will develop along two closely connected directions. First, the successful candidate will work directly with experimentalists to develop rigorous theoretical and computational frameworks for interpreting experimental results and generating testable predictions.

Second, they will investigate simplified and analytically tractable models aimed at identifying general principles governing non-equilibrium chemical reaction networks.

The position is primarily research-oriented. Contributions to teaching activities may be discussed, including the possibility of supervising Master’s students.

Profile

Applicants should have:
• a PhD in physics or related fields, completed or expected to be completed before
the starting date;
• a strong and demonstrated background in statistical mechanics;
• experience with both analytical and computational methods.
Experience with multiphysics simulation software, such as COMSOL or related opensource
or commercial packages, would be considered an asset.
Excellent written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of French is not necessary

We offer

• A stimulating and international working environment

• Competitive salary and excellent working conditions – more information can be found on our website (https://www.epfl.ch/campus/services/human-resources/en/basic-starting-salary-of-doctoral-assistants-and-postdocs/)

• Opportunity to perform state-of-the-art research in one of the most dynamic scientific institutions in Europe.

• Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students

Informations

Applications should include:
1. a one-page motivation letter describing the applicant’s background, research
interests, and relevant experience;
2. a curriculum vitae;
3. contact information for one or two professional references.
The application documents should be submitted via
https://programs-recruiting.epfl.ch/position/49446915
Application deadline is September 15, 2026 but may remain open longer until the
position is filled.
Questions about the position may be addressed to Prof. Paolo De Los Rios at
paolo.delosrios@epfl.ch.

Applications for independent funding will be strongly encouraged and supported.

Contract Start Date : upon mutual agreement, but not earlier than 01.01.2027

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: two years, wi

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Il National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis è un progetto di infrastruttura di ricerca finanziato da SNSF che si concentra sull'esplorazione dell'emergere della vita nell'universo. Questa infrastruttura di ricerca interdisciplinare riunisce fisici, scienziati terrestri e planetari, chimici e biologi per comprendere le condizioni e i meccanismi che permettono alla vita di emergere. Lo sviluppo di metodi affidabili per rilevare tracce affidabili di vita (biosignatures) – sia attraverso il telerilevamento o le misurazioni dirette in loco – richiede una significativa innovazione. Queste sfide richiedono una stretta collaborazione tra fisica, biologia, chimica e scienze della terra. NCCR Genesis non mira a fornire risposte in tutti i campi, ma a guidare la ricerca innovativa e raggiungere un progresso decisivo.

I dettagli sulla genesi NCCR sono disponibili sul suo sito web https://nccr-genesis.ch .

NCCR Genesis è profondamente impegnata per l'uguaglianza, la diversità e l'inclusione. Il nostro obiettivo è quello di coltivare una cultura del lavoro rispettosa ed equa con uguale accesso allo sviluppo professionale e al supporto per tutti. Noi incoraggiamo fortemente le applicazioni da gruppi sottorappresentati.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

Il progetto è condotto in collaborazione con l'Environmental Fluid Mechanics Laboratory (https://pietrodeanna.org) presso l'Università di Losanna, guidata dal Prof. Pietro de Anna, dove si svolgeranno i lavori sperimentali, e con il gruppo di Chimica Teorica dell'ETH di Zurigo (https://reiher.ethz.ch ), guidato dal Prof. Markus Reiher, che eseguirà calcoli quantistici-chimici dettagliati dei tassi di reazione.
La ricerca si svilupperà lungo due direzioni strettamente connesse. In primo luogo, il candidato di successo lavorerà direttamente con gli sperimentatori per sviluppare rigorosi quadri teorici e computazionali per interpretare i risultati sperimentali e generare previsioni testabili.

In secondo luogo, studieranno modelli semplificati e analiticamente trattabili volti a identificare i principi generali che disciplinano le reti di reazione chimica non-equilibrio.

La posizione è principalmente orientata alla ricerca. Possono essere discussi contributi alle attività didattiche, compresa la possibilità di supervisionare gli studenti del Maestro.

Profilo

I candidati dovrebbero avere:
• un dottorato in fisica o campi correlati, completato o previsto di essere completato prima
la data di partenza;

descriptionByLocale.en:
Mission

The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch .

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.

Main duties and responsibilities

The project is conducted in collaboration with the Environmental Fluid Mechanics Laboratory ( https://pietrodeanna.org ) at the University of Lausanne, led by Prof. Pietro de Anna, where the experimental work will be carried out, and with the Theoretical Chemistry group at ETH Zurich ( https://reiher.ethz.ch ), led by Prof. Markus Reiher, which will perform detailed quantum-chemical calculations of reaction rates.
The research will develop along two closely connected directions. First, the successful candidate will work directly with experimentalists to develop rigorous theoretical and computational frameworks for interpreting experimental results and generating testable predictions.

Second, they will investigate simplified and analytically tractable models aimed at identifying general principles governing non-equilibrium chemical reaction networks.

The position is primarily research-oriented. Contributions to teaching activities may be discussed, including the possibility of supervising Master’s students.

Profile

Applicants should have:
• a PhD in physics or related fields, completed or expected to be completed before
the starting date;
• a strong and demonstrated background in statistical mechanics;
• experience with both analytical and computational methods.
Experience with multiphysics simulation software, such as COMSOL or related opensource
or commercial packages, would be considered an asset.
Excellent written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of French is not necessary

We offer

• A stimulating and international working environment

• Competitive salary and excellent working conditions – more information can be found on our website (https://www.epfl.ch/campus/services/human-resources/en/basic-starting-salary-of-doctoral-assistants-and-postdocs/)

• Opportunity to perform state-of-the-art research in one of the most dynamic scientific institutions in Europe.

• Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students

Informations

Applications should include:
1. a one-page motivation letter describing the applicant’s background, research
interests, and relevant experience;
2. a curriculum vitae;
3. contact information for one or two professional references.
The application documents should be submitted via
https://programs-recruiting.epfl.ch/position/49446915
Application deadline is September 15, 2026 but may remain open longer until the
position is filled.
Questions about the position may be addressed to Prof. Paolo De Los Rios at
paolo.delosrios@epfl.ch.

Applications for independent funding will be strongly encouraged and supported.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Das Nationale Forschungskompetenzzentrum NFS Genesis ist ein vom SNF gefördertes Forschungsinfrastrukturprojekt, das sich auf die Erforschung der Entstehung von Leben im Universum konzentriert. Diese interdisziplinäre Forschungsinfrastruktur bringt Physiker, Erd- und Planetenwissenschaftler, Chemiker und Biologen zusammen, um die Bedingungen und Mechanismen zu verstehen, die das Entstehen von Leben ermöglichen. Die Entwicklung zuverlässiger Methoden zur Erkennung zuverlässiger Lebensspuren (Biosignaturen) – sei es durch Fernerkundung oder direkte Messungen vor Ort – erfordert erhebliche Innovationen. Diese Herausforderungen erfordern eine enge Zusammenarbeit zwischen Physik, Biologie, Chemie und den Geowissenschaften. Der NFS Genesis will nicht in allen Bereichen Antworten liefern, sondern innovative Forschung vorantreiben und entscheidende Fortschritte erzielen.

Einzelheiten zum NFS Genesis finden sich auf seiner Website https://nccr-genesis.ch .

Der NFS Genesis setzt sich für Gleichheit, Vielfalt und Inklusion ein. Unser Ziel ist es, eine respektvolle und faire Arbeitskultur mit gleichem Zugang zu beruflicher Entwicklung und Unterstützung für alle zu pflegen. Wir empfehlen dringend Bewerbungen von unterrepräsentierten Gruppen.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Das Projekt wird in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Environmental Fluid Mechanics Laboratory (http://pietrodeanna.org ) an der Universität Lausanne unter der Leitung von Prof. Pietro de Anna, wo die experimentelle Arbeit durchgeführt wird, und mit der Theoretischen Chemie-Gruppe an der ETH Zürich ( https://reiher.ethz.ch ), unter der Leitung von Prof. Markus Reiher, der detaillierte quantenchemische Berechnungen der Reaktionsgeschwindigkeiten durchführen wird.
Die Forschung wird sich in zwei eng miteinander verbundene Richtungen entwickeln. Zunächst wird der erfolgreiche Kandidat direkt mit Experimentatoren zusammenarbeiten, um strenge theoretische und rechnerische Rahmenbedingungen für die Interpretation experimenteller Ergebnisse und die Erzeugung überprüfbarer Vorhersagen zu entwickeln.

Zweitens werden sie vereinfachte und analytisch praktikable Modelle untersuchen, die darauf abzielen, allgemeine Prinzipien für chemische Reaktionsnetzwerke ohne Gleichgewicht zu identifizieren.

Die Position ist in erster Linie forschungsorientiert. Beiträge zu Lehraktivitäten können diskutiert werden, einschließlich der Möglichkeit, Master-Studenten zu beaufsichtigen.

Profil

Antragsteller sollten
• ein PhD in Physik oder verwandten Bereichen, abgeschlossen oder voraussichtlich abgeschlossen, bevor
Startdatum;
• einen starken und nachgewiesenen Hintergrund in der statistischen Mechanik;
• Erfahrung sowohl mit analytischen als auch mit computergestützten Methoden.
Erfahrung mit Multiphysik-Simulationssoftware wie COMSOL oder verwandten OpenSource
oder kommerzielle Pakete, würde als Vermögenswert betrachtet werden.
Hervorragendes geschriebenes und gesprochenes Englisch ist erforderlich. Französischkenntnisse sind nicht notwendig

Wir bieten

• Gelegenheit zur Interaktion mit international renommierten Experten und einem starken Team von Postdoktoranden und Doktoranden

Informationen

Interessen und einschlägige Erfahrungen;

Die Position ist gefüllt.

paolo.delosrios@epfl.ch.

jobs.description:
Your mission

The Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at EPFL is seeking for talented and motivated candidates to work in the field of Integrated Photonics for building fully integrated microcombs for atomic clocks.
This is a part of a European consortium (with UK and Germany) within the QUANTERA funding network.

Atomic clocks are used for precise timing where an accurate knowledge of the absolute time is needed. Based on ultraprecise transitions in atoms, these devices require precise laser control. At the same time, their deployment requires miniaturization away from table-top laser systems towards compact, on-chip laser sources. The aim of this project is a butterfly packaged, soliton-based optical frequency comb (OFC) device which will be used to interrogate a 2-photon Rb based quantum optical clock. Its stabilization requires f-2f frequency locking, and our lab will contribute thin film lithium niobate for this task. Our lab has been making significant progress in developing TFLN photonics for various applications. Building upon these demonstrations, we want to develop periodically poled lithium niobate devices for these metrology tasks.

You will exploit the low-loss thin film lithium niobate photonics platform, which we can fabricate in-house, at EPFL, to realize efficient and low-foot print frequency converters. In parallel, you will study the performance of these devices at frequencies away of the telecom C-band. You will fabricate these hybrid devices in-house at EPFL cleanroom using newly developed fabrication protocols available in the group.

As a successful candidate of a dynamic team, you will shape the future of photonics-based atomic clock technology in our young and dynamic lab. You will push forward our TFLN technology.

You will kick off diverse aspects of the experimental effort: technical (setting up an optical measurement setup design, including multi-frequency setups and custom-tailored mechanical components) and conceptual (develop the theory of frequency conversion inside photonic chips). In the lab, you will learn about integrated and free-space quantum optical technologies and engineering, and nonlinear optics. You will contribute to the automatisation of measurement routines, comprehensive characterisation of fabricated samples and to bridging the area of microwave/terahertz-optical science and technology with the most modern integrated photonic techniques.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop miniaturised frequency converters and apply them to microcombs within the consortium, together with their driving software/hardware, automatize measurement procedures.

• Simulate optical properties using simulations software such as COMSOL or CST.

• Characterize samples in the lab.

• Model experimental data from first principles using Matlab/Python codes.

• Write scientific publications, file patents, disseminate work at national and international conferences.

• Maintain collaborations and deliver periodic reports that describe your progress within the project.

Profile

• M.Sc. in Physics or related fields, strong interest in high-frequency electronics and integrated photonics, nonlinear optics, high-frequency electronics, metrology and/or electro-optic transduction are mandatory.

• Enjoy collaborations with various other scientific groups, take on a leading junior role in international teams.

La tua missione Il Laboratorio Fotonico Ibrido di EPFL è alla ricerca di candidati talentuosi e motivati a lavorare nel campo dei Fotonici Integrati per la costruzione di microcombe completamente integrate per orologi atomici. Questo fa parte di un consorzio europeo (con Regno Unito e Germania) all'interno della rete di finanziamento QUANTERA. Gli orologi atomici sono utilizzati per tempi precisi in cui è necessaria una conoscenza accurata del tempo assoluto. Sulla base di transizioni ultraprecise negli atomi, questi dispositivi richiedono un controllo laser preciso. Allo stesso tempo, la loro distribuzione richiede la miniaturizzazione lontano dai sistemi laser da tavolo verso sorgenti laser compatte e on-chip. L'obiettivo di questo progetto è un dispositivo a farfalla confezionato, solitamenten-based comb di frequenza ottica (OFC) che verrà utilizzato per interrogare un orologio ottico a 2 fotoni basato Rb. La sua stabilizzazione richiede il blocco di frequenza di f-2f, e il nostro laboratorio contribuirà a niobate di litio di pellicola sottile per questo compito. Il nostro laboratorio sta facendo progressi significativi nello sviluppo di fotonici TFLN per varie applicazioni. Basandosi su queste dimostrazioni, vogliamo sviluppare dispositivi di niobate di litio periodicamente inquinati per questi compiti di metrologia. Potrai sfruttare la piattaforma fotonica niobate a basso contenuto di film, che possiamo fabbricare in-house, a EPFL, per realizzare convertitori di frequenza di stampa efficienti e a basso piede. Parallelamente, studierai le prestazioni di questi dispositivi a frequenze lontane dalla banda C di telecomunicazione. Realizzerai questi dispositivi ibridi in-house al cleanroom EPFL utilizzando i protocolli di fabbricazione appena sviluppati disponibili nel gruppo. Come candidato di successo di un team dinamico, formerai il futuro della tecnologia dell'orologio atomico basata su fotonici nel nostro laboratorio giovane e dinamico. Si spingerà avanti la nostra tecnologia TFLN. In laboratorio, imparerai sulle tecnologie ottiche quantiche integrate e free-space e l'ingegneria e l'ottica non lineare. Contribuirai all'automatizzazione delle routine di misura, alla caratterizzazione completa dei campioni fabbricati e alla bridging dell'area della scienza e della tecnologia a microonde/terahertz-ottiche con le più moderne tecniche fotoniche integrate. • Sviluppare convertitori di frequenza miniaturizzati e applicarli a microcombe all'interno del consorzio, insieme al loro software di guida / hardware, automatizzare le procedure di misura.

• M.Sc. in Fisica o campi correlati, forte interesse in elettronica ad alta frequenza e fotonici integrati, ottica non lineare, elettronica ad alta frequenza, metrologia e/o trasduzione elettro-ottica sono obbligatori.

Deine Mission Das Hybrid Photonics Laboratory der EPFL sucht talentierte und motivierte Kandidaten, die im Bereich der integrierten Photonik arbeiten, um vollständig integrierte Mikrokämme für Atomuhren zu bauen. Dies ist Teil eines europäischen Konsortiums (mit Großbritannien und Deutschland) innerhalb des QUANTERA-Fördernetzwerks. Atomuhren werden für ein präzises Timing verwendet, bei dem eine genaue Kenntnis der absoluten Zeit erforderlich ist. Basierend auf ultrapräzisen Übergängen in Atomen erfordern diese Geräte eine präzise Lasersteuerung. Gleichzeitig erfordert ihr Einsatz eine Miniaturisierung weg von Tischlasersystemen hin zu kompakten On-Chip-Laserquellen. Ziel dieses Projekts ist ein mit Schmetterlingen verpacktes OFC-Gerät (Optical Frequency Comb), das zur Abfrage einer optischen 2-Photonen-Rb-basierten Quantenuhr verwendet wird. Seine Stabilisierung erfordert eine f-2f-Frequenzblockierung, und unser Labor wird Dünnfilm-Lithiumniobat für diese Aufgabe beitragen. Unser Labor hat erhebliche Fortschritte bei der Entwicklung der TFLN-Photonik für verschiedene Anwendungen gemacht. Aufbauend auf diesen Demonstrationen wollen wir periodisch gepolte Lithiumniobat-Geräte für diese Messtechnikaufgaben entwickeln. Sie werden die verlustarme Dünnschicht-Lithiumniobat-Photonikplattform nutzen, die wir bei EPFL intern herstellen können, um effiziente und Low-Fuß-Druckfrequenzumrichter zu realisieren. Parallel dazu werden Sie die Leistung dieser Geräte bei Frequenzen außerhalb des Telekommunikations-C-Bands untersuchen. Sie werden diese Hybridgeräte im EPFL-Reinraum mit neu entwickelten Herstellungsprotokollen herstellen, die in der Gruppe verfügbar sind. Im Labor lernen Sie die integrierten und freiraumoptischen Quantentechnologien und -technik sowie die nichtlineare Optik kennen. Votre mission Le Laboratoire de photonique hybride de l'EPFL cherche des candidats talentueux et motivés à travailler dans le domaine de la photonique intégrée pour construire des microcombes entièrement intégrés pour les horloges atomiques. Il fait partie d'un consortium européen (avec le Royaume-Uni et l'Allemagne) au sein du réseau de financement QUANTERA. Les horloges atomiques sont utilisées pour un moment précis où une connaissance précise du temps absolu est nécessaire. Basé sur des transitions ultraprécises dans les atomes, ces dispositifs nécessitent un contrôle laser précis. Dans le même temps, leur déploiement nécessite une miniaturisation loin des systèmes laser de table vers des sources laser compactes sur puce. Le but de ce projet est un appareil de peigne optique de fréquence (OFC) à base de soliton, qui sera utilisé pour interroger une horloge optique quantique à 2 photons Rb. Sa stabilisation nécessite un verrouillage de fréquence f-2f, et notre laboratoire contribuera au niobate de lithium de film mince pour cette tâche. Notre laboratoire a réalisé d'importants progrès dans le développement de la photonique TFLN pour diverses applications. S'appuyant sur ces démonstrations, nous voulons développer périodiquement des dispositifs au lithium niobate pour ces tâches de métrologie. Vous exploiterez la plate-forme de photonique au lithium niobate à faible perte, que nous pouvons fabriquer en interne, à l'EPFL, pour réaliser des convertisseurs de fréquence d'impression à faible intensité. En parallèle, vous étudierez la performance de ces appareils à des fréquences éloignées de la bande C de télécommunication. Vous fabriquerez ces appareils hybrides en interne au salon propre de l'EPFL en utilisant les protocoles de fabrication nouvellement développés disponibles dans le groupe. En tant que candidat reçu d'une équipe dynamique, vous façonnerez l'avenir de la technologie de l'horloge atomique basée sur la photonique dans notre jeune laboratoire dynamique. Vous allez faire avancer notre technologie TFLN. Vous lancerez divers aspects de l'effort expérimental : technique (mise en place d'une configuration de mesure optique, y compris des configurations multifréquences et des composants mécaniques personnalisés) et conceptuelle (développement de la théorie de la conversion de fréquence à l'intérieur des puces photoniques). Au laboratoire, vous apprendrez sur les technologies et l'ingénierie quantiques intégrées et libres, ainsi que sur l'optique non linéaire. Vous contribuerez à l'automatisation des routines de mesure, à la caractérisation complète des échantillons fabriqués et à l'intégration des techniques photoniques intégrées les plus modernes dans le domaine de la science et de la technologie micro-ondes/terahertz. • Simuler les propriétés optiques à l'aide de logiciels de simulation tels que COMSOL ou CST.

jobs.description:
Mission

The Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at EPFL is seeking for talented and motivated candidates to join our growing team in the field of Integrated Photonics for generation of high-quality electronic signals at elevated frequencies beyond 100 GHz. This is a collaborative project with IEMN Lille as part of a Swiss-French collaborative project.
High-end microwave instrumentation is at the core of communications, computing, metrology, sensing or ranging. Yet, it relies on the availability of broadband tunable, narrow linewidth, and bright microwave sources that can be used to excite a high-frequency circuit or to detect its response via heterodyne techniques.

You will research hybrid photonic-spintronic chips on silicon nitride, an offering integrated photonic platform providing ultra low-loss, negligible two-photon absorption, high optical nonlinearity, possibilities to engineer both positive and negative group velocity dispersion through waveguide design and high-Finesse optical resonators, with the aim to develop compact and efficient sources of pulsed and continuous wave terahertz radiation in the band from 100 GHz to 10 THz.

jobs.description:
Mission

The Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) is looking for a PhD student for our Antarctica InSync activities. Within Antarctica InSync we will study aerosol-cloud interactions over coastal Antarctica and the Southern Ocean sea ice with instruments placed on a tethered balloon and at ground.

Your mission will be to perform and analyze vertically resolved measurements of aerosols, trace gases and meteorological variables using EERL’s helikite facility and to conduct ground based aerosol chemical observations using the new nano-mechanical membrane infrared spectroscopy method (NEMS-FTIR) that we developed.

The EERL focuses on understanding natural and anthropogenic atmospheric processes, as well as exchange processes between the atmosphere and cryosphere, ocean and land that have climate impact and are impacted by climate. Within Antarctica InSync, the EERL will deploy instruments on the icebreaker Polarstern that will drift in the Weddell Sea and at Neumayer station as part of the DOMINO project.

Main tasks and responsibilities

• Perform field observations with a small team in Antarctica using the helikite facility

• Enhance the helikite's measurement capabilities by adding new instrumentation for chemical analyses and cloud observations with the support of a technician

• Analyze samples of aerosols and trace gases in laboratory, for e.g., chemical composition and ice nucleating particles

• Data analysis of observations, numerical model output and remote sensing data

• Tight collaboration with the project partners and participation in working meetings

• Teaching assistantship

• Part-time supervision of MSc students

Profile

• A master degree or (equivalent) in atmospheric, climate, or environment science, engineering, meteorology, physics or similar

• Interest in atmospheric studies and polar regions

• Desire to do field work

• Desire to do laboratory work

• Interested in improving the tethered balloon payload with support of EERL's technician

• Capable of conducting scientific research independently

• Basic knowledge of scientific programming

• Data handling skills

• Good interpersonal skills, team player

• Good knowlege of English (written and spoken)

We offer

• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and young research group

• A vibrant, internationally visible and rising academic institution in alpine and polar environments research

• A great working atmosphere and ample opportunities for professional and personal development with access to many continuing education courses

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering ( EDCE ). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position.

Your application should contain: A motivation Letter, Your detailed CV, Contact information, The names and contact information of 3 references willing to write a recommendation letter

For the application, you must submit your documents in two places (Please check this page for additional information on admission) .:

1) Via the EPFL recruitment platform: Please submit a motivation letter with your interests and qualifications, a CV and publication list (if applicable), your bachelor and master curriculum with grades, and contacts of three references.

2) Please ensure to submit as well an application to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position. The submission deadline for EDCE is September 15, 2026.

Please note, PhD positions are awarded initially for one year. After one year of successful probation, the initial contract can be extended up to a total of four years.

Application deadline: 15/09/2026

Contract Start Date: 01/10/2026

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Il Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) è alla ricerca di uno studente di dottorato per le nostre attività in Antartide InSync. All'interno dell'Antartide InSync studieremo interazioni aerosol-cloud sull'Antartide costiera e sul ghiaccio marino dell'Oceano Meridionale con strumenti posti su un palloncino tethered e a terra.

La vostra missione sarà di eseguire e analizzare le misurazioni verticalmente risolte di aerosol, gas di traccia e variabili meteorologiche utilizzando la struttura elikite di EERL e di condurre osservazioni chimiche aerosol a terra utilizzando il nuovo metodo di spettroscopia a membrana nano-meccanica infrarossi (NEMS-FTIR) che abbiamo sviluppato.

L'EERL si concentra sulla comprensione dei processi atmosferici naturali e antropogeni, nonché sui processi di scambio tra l'atmosfera e la criosfera, l'oceano e la terra che hanno un impatto climatico e sono influenzati dal clima. All'interno dell'Antartide InSync, l'EERL distribuirà strumenti sul rompicapo Polarstern che andrà alla deriva nel Mar di Weddell e nella stazione di Neumayer come parte del progetto DOMINO.

Principali compiti e responsabilità

• Eseguire osservazioni sul campo con una piccola squadra in Antartide utilizzando la struttura helikite

• Migliorare le capacità di misura dell'elikite aggiungendo una nuova strumentazione per analisi chimiche e osservazioni sul cloud con il supporto di un tecnico

• Analizzare campioni di aerosol e di gas di traccia in laboratorio, per esempio, composizione chimica e particelle di ghiaccio

• Analisi dei dati delle osservazioni, dell'output del modello numerico e del rilevamento remoto dei dati

• stretta collaborazione con i partner del progetto e partecipazione alle riunioni di lavoro

• Assistente didattico

• Supervisione part-time degli studenti MSc

Profilo

• Una laurea magistrale o (equivalente) in scienze atmosferiche, climatiche o ambientali, ingegneria, meteorologia, fisica o simili

• Interessi degli studi atmosferici e delle regioni polari

• Desiderio fare lavoro sul campo

• Desiderio fare lavoro di laboratorio

• Interessato a migliorare il carico utile del palloncino con il supporto del tecnico di EERL

• Capacità di condurre la ricerca scientifica in modo indipendente

• Conoscenza di base della programmazione scientifica

• Capacità di gestione dei dati

• Buone abilità interpersonali, giocatore di squadra

• Buona conoscenza dell'inglese (scritto e parlato)

Offriamo

• Un gruppo di ricerca dinamico, interdisciplinare e giovane

• Un'istituzione accademica vibrante, visibile a livello internazionale e in crescita nella ricerca di ambienti alpini e polari

• Una grande atmosfera di lavoro e ampie opportunità di sviluppo professionale e personale con accesso a molti corsi di formazione continua

• 4 anni per completare il dottorato con una remunerazione competitiva

• Un contratto a tempo determinato di 1 anno (CDD), rinnovabile per 4 anni

Informazioni

Il processo di selezione coinvolge più fasi, e candidati a lista corta saranno richiesti per applicare al programma di dottorato in ingegneria civile e ambientale (EDCE ). Solo i candidati ammessi all'EDCE possono essere considerati per questa posizione.

La vostra domanda dovrebbe contenere: Una lettera di motivazione, il vostro CV dettagliato, informazioni di contatto, i nomi e le informazioni di contatto di 3 riferimenti disposti a scrivere una lettera di raccomandazione

Per l'applicazione, è necessario inviare i documenti in due posti (Si prega di controllare questa pagina per ulteriori informazioni sull'ammissione) .:

1) Attraverso la piattaforma di reclutamento EPFL: Si prega di inviare una lettera di motivazione con i vostri interessi e qualifiche, un CV e una lista di pubblicazione (se applicabile), il vostro curriculum di laurea e master con voti, e contatti di tre referenze.

2) Assicurarsi di presentare anche una domanda al programma di dottorato in ingegneria civile e ambientale (EDCE). Solo i candidati ammessi all'EDCE possono essere considerati per questa posizione. Il termine di presentazione per EDCE è il 15 settembre 2026.

Si prega di notare, le posizioni di dottorato sono assegnati inizialmente per un anno. Dopo un anno di prova di successo, il contratto iniziale può essere esteso fino a un totale di quattro anni.

Termine per la richiesta: 15/09/2026

Data di inizio del contratto: 01/10/2026

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Das Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) sucht einen Doktoranden für unsere InSync Aktivitäten in der Antarktis. Innerhalb von Antarctica InSync werden wir Aerosol-Cloud-Wechselwirkungen über der Küstenantarktis und dem Meereis des Südpolarmeers mit Instrumenten untersuchen, die auf einem angebundenen Ballon und am Boden platziert sind.

Ihre Mission wird es sein, vertikal aufgelöste Messungen von Aerosolen, Spurengasen und meteorologischen Variablen mit der Helikit-Anlage von EERL durchzuführen und zu analysieren und bodenbasierte Aerosol-chemische Beobachtungen mit der neuen nanomechanischen Infrarot-Membranspektroskopie-Methode (NEMS-FTIR) durchzuführen, die wir entwickelt haben.

Das EERL konzentriert sich auf das Verständnis natürlicher und anthropogener atmosphärischer Prozesse sowie Austauschprozesse zwischen Atmosphäre und Kryosphäre, Ozean und Land, die sich auf das Klima auswirken und vom Klima beeinflusst werden. Innerhalb von Antarctica InSync wird das EERL Instrumente auf dem Eisbrecher Polarstern einsetzen, der im Weddellmeer und an der Station Neumayer im Rahmen des DOMINO-Projekts treiben wird.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

• Führen Sie Feldbeobachtungen mit einem kleinen Team in der Antarktis mit Hilfe der Helikit-Anlage durch

• Verbessern Sie die Messfähigkeit des Helikits durch Hinzufügen neuer Instrumente für chemische Analysen und Wolkenbeobachtungen mit Unterstützung eines Technikers

• Analyse von Proben von Aerosolen und Spurengasen im Labor, z. B. für die chemische Zusammensetzung und Eiskeimpartikel

• Datenanalyse von Beobachtungen, numerische Modellausgabe und Fernerkundungsdaten

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit den Projektpartnern und Teilnahme an Arbeitstreffen

• Lehrassistenz

• Teilzeitaufsicht von MSc-Studenten

Profil

• Ein Master-Abschluss oder (äquivalent) in Atmosphären-, Klima- oder Umweltwissenschaften, Ingenieurwissenschaften, Meteorologie, Physik oder ähnlichem

• Interesse an atmosphärischen Studien und Polarregionen

• Wunsch, Feldarbeit zu machen

• Wunsch nach Laborarbeit

• Interesse an der Verbesserung der Nutzlast des angebundenen Ballons mit Unterstützung des EERL-Technikers

• Fähigkeit zur unabhängigen Durchführung wissenschaftlicher Forschung

• Grundkenntnisse der wissenschaftlichen Programmierung

• Fähigkeiten im Umgang mit Daten

• Gute zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten, Teamplayer

• Gute Englischkenntnisse (geschrieben und gesprochen)

Wir bieten

• Eine dynamische, interdisziplinäre und junge Forschungsgruppe

• Eine lebendige, international sichtbare und aufstrebende akademische Institution in der alpinen und polaren Umweltforschung

• Eine gute Arbeitsatmosphäre und reichlich Möglichkeiten zur beruflichen und persönlichen Entwicklung mit Zugang zu vielen Weiterbildungskursen

• 4 Jahre, um Ihre PhD mit einer wettbewerbsfähigen Vergütung abzuschließen

• Ein 1-jähriger befristeter Vertrag (CDD), erneuerbar für 4 Jahre

Informationen

Der Auswahlprozess umfasst mehrere Phasen, und die in die engere Auswahl genommenen Kandidaten werden aufgefordert, sich für das Doktorandenprogramm in Bau- und Umwelttechnik (EDCE) zu bewerben. Nur Bewerber, die zur EDCE zugelassen sind, können für diese Position in Betracht gezogen werden.

Ihre Bewerbung sollte Folgendes enthalten: Ein Motivationsschreiben, Ihren detaillierten Lebenslauf, Kontaktinformationen, die Namen und Kontaktinformationen von 3 Referenzen, die bereit sind, ein Empfehlungsschreiben zu schreiben.

Nur Bewerber, die zur EDCE zugelassen sind, können für diese Position in Betracht gezogen werden. Die Einreichungsfrist für EDCE ist der 15. September 2026.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

The Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) is looking for a PhD student for our Antarctica InSync activities. Within Antarctica InSync we will study aerosol-cloud interactions over coastal Antarctica and the Southern Ocean sea ice with instruments placed on a tethered balloon and at ground.

Your mission will be to perform and analyze vertically resolved measurements of aerosols, trace gases and meteorological variables using EERL’s helikite facility and to conduct ground based aerosol chemical observations using the new nano-mechanical membrane infrared spectroscopy method (NEMS-FTIR) that we developed.

The EERL focuses on understanding natural and anthropogenic atmospheric processes, as well as exchange processes between the atmosphere and cryosphere, ocean and land that have climate impact and are impacted by climate. Within Antarctica InSync, the EERL will deploy instruments on the icebreaker Polarstern that will drift in the Weddell Sea and at Neumayer station as part of the DOMINO project.

Main tasks and responsibilities

• Perform field observations with a small team in Antarctica using the helikite facility

• Enhance the helikite's measurement capabilities by adding new instrumentation for chemical analyses and cloud observations with the support of a technician

• Analyze samples of aerosols and trace gases in laboratory, for e.g., chemical composition and ice nucleating particles

• Data analysis of observations, numerical model output and remote sensing data

• Tight collaboration with the project partners and participation in working meetings

• Teaching assistantship

• Part-time supervision of MSc students

Profile

• A master degree or (equivalent) in atmospheric, climate, or environment science, engineering, meteorology, physics or similar

• Interest in atmospheric studies and polar regions

• Desire to do field work

• Desire to do laboratory work

• Interested in improving the tethered balloon payload with support of EERL's technician

• Capable of conducting scientific research independently

• Basic knowledge of scientific programming

• Data handling skills

• Good interpersonal skills, team player

• Good knowlege of English (written and spoken)

We offer

• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and young research group

• A vibrant, internationally visible and rising academic institution in alpine and polar environments research

• A great working atmosphere and ample opportunities for professional and personal development with access to many continuing education courses

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering ( EDCE ). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position.

Your application should contain: A motivation Letter, Your detailed CV, Contact information, The names and contact information of 3 references willing to write a recommendation letter

For the application, you must submit your documents in two places (Please check this page for additional information on admission) .:

1) Via the EPFL recruitment platform: Please submit a motivation letter with your interests and qualifications, a CV and publication list (if applicable), your bachelor and master curriculum with grades, and contacts of three references.

2) Please ensure to submit as well an application to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position. The submission deadline for EDCE is September 15, 2026.

Please note, PhD positions are awarded initially for one year. After one year of successful probation, the initial contract can be extended up to a total of four years.

jobs.description:
Mission

Within the faculty of engineering (STI), the Galatea Laboratory explores novel paradigms to tailor material properties locally using lasers. Our research involves three main clusters: understanding and exploring laser-matter interaction phenomena, investigating new manufacturing processes based on 3D direct-write laser methods, and finally, exploring novel concepts of multi-scale systems based on single monolith. The lab features state-of-the-art laser facilities and infrastructure for pioneer research.

The Galatea Lab is located in the vibrant Neuchâtel’s campus of EPFL, part of Microcity, a ecosystem with a focused on micro-technologies.

To strengthen our research program on laser-based methods to tailor material properties, we are looking for a post-doc to investigate advanced wavefront shaping methods based on adaptive optics applied to the context of nonlinear laser-matter interaction.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Define relevant research and experimental plans, sustained with theoretical considerations and knowledge of the relevant literature.

• Conduct experiments and analyze data.

• Report and disseminate the research outcome in journal publications and at international conferences.

• Interact and collaborate with other lab members as well as with industrial partners.

• Occasionally supervise undergraduate students (bachelor or master levels).

• Contribute to the laboratory operations through shared duties.

Profile

• You recently obtained a PhD in optics, applied physics or related fields with a strong knowledge of optics.

• You have experience in adaptive optics as well as hands-on experience with optical setups involving lasers.

• You have a keen interest in research in the field of nonlinear optics, ultrafast lasers and/or laser-matter interaction.

• You are independent, creative, solution-oriented, flexible and a team-player.

We offer

• Opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge emerging research topics.

• Opportunity to work in an established multidisciplinary lab in ultrafast laser-matter interaction and advanced manufacturing processes, as well as optomechanical designs.

• Opportunity to access state-of-the-art research facilities and laboratory resources.

• Opportunity to collaborate with world-leading research groups through international collaborations.

• Opportunity to interact with multidisciplinary projects with strong links to industry and spin-offs.

• EPFL is an international and top-ranking university. It offers a young, stimulating, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and international working environment, a broad range of scientific training and networking events and hosts a vibrant entrepreneurial community.

• EPFL is an equal-opportunity employer. Candidates will be recruited solely based on merit.

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered.

A brief cover letter (pdf, up to 2 pages).

And in one PDF:

A CV with a publication list.
A research statement (pdf, up to 3 pages).
Contact details for 3 referees.

For any further information, please contact: prof. Yves Bellouard - yves.bellouard@epfl.ch

Keywords: Adaptive optics, beam shaping, nonlinear optics, laser-matter interaction, ultrafast lasers.

jobs.description:
Mission

The Zenk Lab (NeuroNA Chair in Epigenomics of Neurodevelopmental disorders – EpiGN) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with strong training in computational biology and/or machine learning to join an interdisciplinary project at the interface of single-cell genomics, data integration, and developmental biology.
The project focuses on the integration and analysis of multi-modal single-cell datasets, including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, scCUT&Tag, HiC, and proteomics, with an emphasis on trajectory inference, regulatory dynamics, and cell fate decisions. • Experience with machine learning and/or statistical modeling applied to biological data

• Proven expertise in single-cell data analysis (scRNA-seq and/or scATAC-seq)

• Interest or experience in multi-modal data integration and trajectory inference

• Proficiency in Python and/or R

• Interest in developmental and human biology is highly valued, but not required

• Strong collaborative mindset and ability to work across disciplines

We offer

• Close collaboration with leading groups in single-cell genomics and machine learning
